codecs.note: this build DOES carry hardware decoders, which contradicts the assumption in §5.5 that a PyPI wheel would not. That makes B9 cheaper than planned but not free: asking for a cuvid decoder still ends with to_ndarray copying the frame back to host memory, so the PCIe round trip §5.5 actually cares about survives until the ONNX IO-binding refactor. Nothing to do here; B4 is about PTS.

timeline_fidelity.verdict: variable rate: a duration of up to 30 s can be misstated by 0.81 s on the derived timeline. Measure this recording with ingest.backend: pyav, and do not compare gap lengths taken on the two timelines

opencv.note: cv2.VideoCapture discards the container PTS, so the only timeline available from this backend is frame_index / reported_fps (§5.5).

frame_count_agreement.note: both decoders saw the same number of frames

rate_declaration.note: average_rate != guessed_rate is the variable-rate signature: the container nominally runs at guessed_rate and actually delivered fewer frames. cv2 reports the average, so the derived timeline is right on average and wrong locally.

decode_timing.method: one discarded warm-up pass per backend, then interleaved timed passes; median reported
decode_timing.conclusion: OpenCV is 27.5% faster, which is outside the 8.8% run-to-run spread. If that is PyAV losing, it is per-frame Python overhead and should be fixed rather than accepted.
